chunks: Ahmad ibn Harun (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from his father Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami', from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:
If a depraved person openly declares his depravity, then he has no sanctity and there is no backbiting [regarding him].

key_terms.الفاسق: Fasiq - a depraved or sinful person who transgresses divine law
key_terms.جاهر: Jahara - to declare openly, to make public, to be brazen about
key_terms.حرمة: Hurmah - sanctity, inviolability, the protected status of a person's honor
key_terms.غيبة: Ghiba - backbiting, speaking about someone in their absence in a way they would dislike

ai.seo_question: Is backbiting permissible against someone who openly sins in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a jurisprudential principle regarding backbiting (ghiba): when a person openly and shamelessly displays sinful behavior, the prohibition of backbiting does not apply to them. In Islamic ethics, backbiting is normally a grave sin (cf. Quran 49:12), but this hadith carves out an exception for those who publicly flaunt their transgressions, as they have forfeited the right to reputation protection by their own open conduct.
